heroHeadline: Egypt's FM Warns of Economic 'Perfect Storm' From Gaza War and Hormuz Blockade; Sisi Hosts Haftar and Qatar's PM as Sinai Pipeline Spill Is Contained
heroSubtitle: Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty said on August 25, 2026 that Egypt's economy faces 'a perfect storm' from the combined toll of the Gaza war, the Strait of Hormuz blockade, and Houthi Red Sea attacks, which have cost the Suez Canal roughly $11 billion in lost revenue — even as he cited 5.5% growth and large reserves as signs of resilience. Earlier in the week, Abdelatty condemned Israel's E1 West Bank settlement project and discussed Hormuz maritime security with Oman in a round of regional diplomacy on August 22. President Sisi received Libyan National Army commander Khalifa Haftar on August 19 to reaffirm support for Libyan unity and elections, and hosted Qatar's Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman on August 20 for the seventh Egyptian-Qatari Joint Higher Committee, setting October talks on a bilateral economic partnership agreement. On August 26, Egyptian authorities announced they had contained a crude oil pipeline spill off Ras Badran in South Sinai after slicks reached a public beach near Abu Rudeis.
footerNote: Data sourced from Egyptian official records, UNESCO, academic Egyptology research (Shaw, Lehner, Hawass), major international outlets, IMF, Human Rights Watch, and institutional analyses.
